transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Pathfinder CTO), Emily Chen (Pathfinder ML Eng), Luis Martinez (Pathfinder Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Maya from our SE team. Quick round — Samir you mentioned you were in SF but dialing in remote?
[00:10] Samir: Yeah, I'm on the east coast today but all good, thanks for organizing.
[00:15] Maya: Hi all, I'll jump into the technical details later — intent is to understand your stack and then go deep on compatibility and benchmarks.

Summary / Goals portion:
[00:30] Jordan: For today's call we want to understand your current OpenAI usage, what workloads are highest priority, constraints on latency/cost/compliance, and what success looks like for migration. We'll also capture next steps for a bench and security review.

Discovery - current setup:
[01:05] Samir: Quick background — Pathfinder runs a hybrid product: real-time assistant for analysts and nightly batch embedding/index builds. Right now we use OpenAI — mostly gpt-4o-ish endpoints for chat and text-generation, and ada/embedding endpoints for vectors. Peak concurrency is around 200 concurrent chat sessions during market hours, typically 35-40 requests/s average, with spikes up to 120 rps for short periods. Token volumes are heavy — maybe 3-4M tokens/day.
[01:40] Emily: Our models are relatively prompt-heavy — we do multi-turn context, synthetic system prompts, and we also run a reranker step using a custom reranker model hosted on TGI internally for experimentation.
[02:05] Maya: Got it. So two main flows: low-latency chat and offline embedding/indexing. For Dedicated we can separate pools, or use Dedicated for chat and Hosted for embeddings if you want to start hybrid. Any hard constraints on PII or data residency?
[02:25] Samir: We can't persist PII in third-party storage; embeddings are okay to store in our AWS account. Main ask is auditability and key control — KMS, SSO, RBAC, and logs.

Technical compatibility concerns (vLLM / TGI / eval parity):
[03:05] Emily: The big blocker for us is eval/regression parity. We ran some experiments with vLLM and TGI; outputs shifted slightly and our reranker sometimes prefers the original OpenAI outputs. We need to make sure model behavior is consistent or that we can measure and accept the deltas.
[03:30] Maya: Right, eval parity is a classic one. A few notes — Redwood Dedicated runs the same open checkpoint (we can pin versions), and we usually match tokenizer and sampling params. But downstream infra like vLLM's scheduling or TGI's custom kernels can change timing and sometimes tokenization bucketing. We'll want your canonical prompt set to run side-by-side.
[03:55] Samir: Is there a known delta when moving from OpenAI hosted to a self-hosted variant? Our initial tests showed lower hallucination on OpenAI in some prompts, weirdly.
[04:10] Maya: Could be due to temperature/sampling differences, or the model variant. Also OpenAI often uses proprietary fine-tuning. For open checkpoints we recommend doing A/B evals on your metrics (F1, factuality, downstream signal), and Redwood can run the bench.
[04:30] Emily: Also curious about stateful sessions — our chat sessions use a KV cache and we care about latency for token streaming. Does Redwood Dedicated support prefix/KV caching for faster turn times?
[04:45] Maya: Yes, our serving runtime supports KV cache reuse and prefix caching to reduce compute for repeated context. We also have continuous batching but with latency SLO config so you can set a cap for real-time requests.

Security & Compliance discussion:
[05:10] Luis: From security side we need SSO (SAML/OIDC), per-team RBAC, audit logs, and encryption at rest with our KMS. Also need to understand network isolation — VPC peering or private link, and whether data ever touches Redwood-managed buckets.
[05:30] Jordan: For Dedicated we offer customer-dedicated GPU pools and optional VPC connectors — logs and telemetry can be forwarded to your account. We also support customer KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping. We'll send a security pack with SOC 2 and ISO artifacts.
[05:48] Luis: Is there any onboarding that requires us to upload data to Redwood S3? We prefer zero-touch storage on your side.
[05:58] Maya: You can run Dedicated in a VPC with no managed buckets; we can also do a private deployment where control plane is customer-managed if needed. We'll detail options in the pack.

Benchmarks and performance expectations:
[07:10] Jordan: For cost/throughput, do you have current per-token costs or monthly spend with OpenAI?
[07:18] Samir: Ballpark $25k per month across teams but it's spiky. Latency SLOs: p50 around 150-200ms for single-turn chat, p95 ideally <400ms. For embeddings batch is less sensitive.
[07:35] Maya: Dedicated gives predictability — reserved capacity with autoscaling. For similar latency we typically recommend quantization profiles and batching configs tuned to your seq lengths. For actual numbers we'd like to run a benchmark with your prompts and traffic profile.
[07:55] Emily: One thing — our reranker stage uses TGI on CPU for cheap runs; if we move the primary generation to Dedicated GPUs, will it play nice with our reranker chain? We need easy integration and consistent outputs.
[08:14] Maya: Yes, the runtime has API parity for generation calls; you'll still orchestrate reranker as a downstream job. If you want we can co-locate reranker on the same Dedicated cluster (if supported) or keep it in your infra and just pass tokens. We'll map the end-to-end latency in the bench.

Specific migration questions & gotchas:
[09:00] Samir: Our engineers tried to run TGI/vLLM and saw tokenization mismatches — sometimes newlines and special tokens changed scoring. Does Redwood offer a tokenizer compatibility guide?
[09:15] Maya: We do. Most issues come from different tokenizer versions or pre-token normalization. We can share a checklist: tokenizers, model configs, sampling params, and deterministic seeds where possible. Also recommend running a small subset of prompts to catch edge-cases.
[09:30] Emily: For eval parity, how do you recommend we instrument tests? We have unit tests and human evals — but need automated regression alerts if quality dips after migration.
[09:42] Maya: Redwood Optimize can hook into your evals and alert on regressions tied to prompt sets. For an initial migration, run A/B tests with your metric suite and set thresholds — we'll help configure alerts.

Pricing & contracts (high level):
[10:10] Jordan: Pricing will be a mix of reserved capacity for Dedicated plus overage. We can send a few scenarios (small pilot, 1x production, high-availability). Any constraints on budget timing?
[10:22] Samir: We want to pilot in Q4 and then decide by mid-Q1. Budget is approx $200k for FY27 but that covers multiple infra changes — we need firm numbers for reserved nodes.

Integration and onboarding timeline:
[11:00] Jordan: Typical flow — pilot with a small reserved pool, run bench and canary on a fraction of traffic, then expand. Pilot is 4-6 weeks from kick-off depending on prompt set and benchmarks.
[11:12] Samir: That aligns — we can carve out a team to support this.

Live Q&A (noise, cross-talk):
[11:30] Emily: Quick question — if we keep embeddings in our AWS, is there a recommended way to encrypt them with our keys?
[11:36] Maya: Use your KMS to encrypt at rest; we can accept encrypted payloads and we support key-wrap patterns. We'll add an architecture note in the security pack.
[11:45] Luis: Audit retention — can we export audit logs to our SIEM?
[11:49] Maya: Yes, logs can be streamed to your endpoint, and we have configurable retention.

Deep technical detail (Maya elaborates):
[12:20] Maya: On runtime specifics — we do kernel selection at runtime based on sequence length distribution, and we support INT8/4 quant profiles. For streaming we have a low-latency path that minimizes tokenization overhead. vLLM's scheduling can be more aggressive on overlapping I/O which sometimes yields different P95. We'll model your distribution and tune.
[12:50] Emily: For the quantized models you mentioned — we need to confirm they don't change the logits distribution in ways that affect downstream reranking. What's the rollback story?
[13:05] Maya: We version models and pin rollouts; we recommend canarying quant profiles and keeping the float baseline available so you can fail back quickly. Redwood Console exposes per-model token-level statistics so you can compare.

Objections and mitigations:
[14:10] Samir: Our execs worry about the migration effort and the risk of a regression mid-Q1.
[14:20] Jordan: That's why we propose a staged pilot: run your exact prompts and metric suite in parallel, quantify deltas, and have rollback policies. We'll also include an SLA for Dedicated.

Wrap-up and explicit next steps:
[15:00] Jordan: Recap — we will: (1) send Dedicated pricing + pilot options, (2) Maya sends benchmark plan and tokenizer compatibility checklist, (3) security pack goes to Luis, (4) schedule technical deep dive with infra. Does that capture it?
[15:15] Samir: Yep, that works. Can we aim to have the pilot started first week of November?
[15:20] Jordan: Yes, target week of Nov 2. We'll send invites.

Action items repeated:
[15:30] Jordan: Jordan - share pricing + onboarding guide by Oct 29. Maya - request canonical prompt set and bench plan by Nov 3. Samir - share sample prompts and compliance list by Oct 30.

End notes (small transcription noise and filler):
[15:45] Speaker 1: mm-hm, okay thanks, cool.
[16:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts. Bye.
